questions.question: What will this code print?
questions.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(8, activation='relu', input_shape=(4,)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)
])
print(model.layers[0].get_weights()[0].shape)
questions.explanation: The first Dense layer has 4 inputs and 8 units, so its kernel shape is (4, 8).

questions.question: What is the shape of the output after this convolution?
questions.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Conv2D
conv = Conv2D(32, (3,3), padding='same', input_shape=(32,32,3))
x = tf.random.normal((1,32,32,3))
print(conv(x).shape)
questions.explanation: With padding='same', spatial size remains 32×32. Output depth equals number of filters (32).

questions.question: What does this LSTM output shape print?
questions.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.layers import LSTM
lstm = LSTM(64, return_sequences=False, input_shape=(10, 8))
x = tf.random.normal((5,10,8))  # batch=5, timesteps=10, features=8
print(lstm(x).shape)
questions.explanation: With `return_sequences=False`, only the last output is returned, shape (batch, units) = (5, 64).

questions.question: What will the printed loss value approximately be? (Hint: perfect predictions)
questions.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf
loss_fn = tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy()
y_true = tf.constant([[1.], [0.]])
y_pred = tf.constant([[0.99], [0.01]])
print(loss_fn(y_true, y_pred).numpy().round(3))
questions.explanation: Binary cross‑entropy: -[1*log(0.99) + (1-0)*log(1-0.01)] / 2 ≈ -[ -0.01005 + -0.01005]/2 ≈ 0.01005, the actual value around 0.005 after averaging. The rounding gives 0.005.
